channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Google Cloud Warns Three AMD Turin CPU Flaws Could Leak Data Across Processes in VMs
item.description: Google Cloud VMs on AMD Turin chips need a guest OS patch and a stop-and-start to protect against three CPU side-channel flaws, Google said this week. Inside a VM, the flaws may let an attacker with code on the same processor core infer data from other processes or the kernel.

item.title: Exploit Attempts for GPUStack Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-102895), (Thu, Nov 12th)
item.description: CVE-2026-102895 is a trivial authentication-bypass vulnerability. All versions of GPUStack prior to 2.2.0, which was released at the end of June. This vulnerability was not made public until the end of July, and the CVE was assigned on November 4th.

item.title: RHEL 10 Receives RPM Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for rpm on Red Enterprise Linux 10, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The advisory rates the update as Moderate, with CVSS base scores available via CVE links in the references. Defenders should apply the rpm patch to mitigate the identified critical weaknesses and maintain system integrity.

item.title: New N-central Exploits Work Against Patched Servers, Enable Root RCE and Windows SYSTEM Access
item.description: N-able on Thursday said it's investigating a new public disclosure containing claims of additional vulnerabilities in on-premise versions of N-central running version 2026.4.1 HF2. "Based on our initial review, the server issue described depends on a non-default configuration in which the Legacy API is turned on and exposed to the public internet," N-able said in a new advisory.

item.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
item.description: Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users. Every check defenders normally lean on to judge a link came back clean, and the operator designed it that way on purpose.

item.title: RHEL 10 Receives Cockpit Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for cockpit on Red Enterprise Linux 10, addressing several vulnerabilities. The advisory rates the update as Important, with CVSS base scores linked to CVE references for each flaw. Defenders should apply the cockpit patch promptly to prevent exploitation and preserve critical system security overall.

item.title: RHSA-2026:99603: Important: cockpit security update
item.description: An update for cockpit is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: RHSA-2026:99597: Important: gdb security update
item.description: An update for gdb is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 Advanced Mission Critical Update Support and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.6 Extended Update Support Long-Life Add-On. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important.

item.title: PTC Patches Critical Windchill and FlexPLM Flaw That Could Enable Remote Code Execution
item.description: PTC has released patches for a new critical vulnerability impacting Windchill and FlexPLM software that, if successfully exploited, could result in remote code execution. The security flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-126325, carries a CVSS v4 score of 9.2 out of a maximum of 10.0.

item.title: AI Scripts Enable Rapid Lateral Movement in Retail Breach
item.description: An attacker used AI-generated scripts after hand-typed commands failed to breach a US retailer. The AI scripts facilitated lateral movement within minutes, indicating a rapid compromise of internal systems and exposing sensitive data. Security teams should investigate compromised accounts, isolate affected segments, review AI-based attack mitigations, and strengthen monitoring immediately.

item.title: ScreenConnect Extension Vulnerability Enables Malware
item.description: Hackers exploited a flaw in a legitimate ScreenConnect extension to bypass authentication and deploy malware. The flaw lets attackers bypass ScreenConnect’s login controls, granting unauthorized session access; no CVE is listed and exploitation is confined to the extension. ScreenConnect has released an update patching the extension; administrators should apply the latest version and verify extension integrity.

item.title: Red Hat Issues OpenSSH Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released an OpenSSH update for RHEL 8.4 Advanced Mission Critical and Extended Update Support, addressing multiple SSH vulnerabilities. Each flaw’s CVSS base score is listed in the references, indicating severity ranges but no confirmed exploitation. Apply the patch immediately to prevent potential remote code execution and maintain SSH service integrity.

item.title: N-able Rushes Patches for Exploited N-central Zero-Days
item.description: Threat actors are actively targeting zero-day vulnerabilities within N-able N-central remote management software following recent public disclosures. The malicious campaign surfaced shortly after a security researcher publicly dropped over 30 zero-day flaws affecting the enterprise management platform. In response to active threat activity, N-able released urgent patches specifically addressing the unauthenticated security vulnerabilities.

item.title: Threat Actors Use GSocket for Persistent Linux Access
item.description: Threat actors use the open‑source remote tool GSocket to keep access on Linux servers after patching initial exploitation vulnerabilities. This persistence method lets attackers re‑establish control even when known flaws are fixed, bypassing patch‑based defenses. Defenders should detect GSocket binaries, enforce whitelisting, and apply vendor patches to close this vector.

item.title: Red Hat Issues libX11 Security Update for RHEL 8.8
item.description: Red Hat released a libX11 security update for RHEL 8.8 SAP and Telecommunications services, fixing multiple X11 client library vulnerabilities. The patch is rated Important, with CVSS base scores provided via CVE references, though no active exploitation has been reported. Red Hat advises immediate installation to prevent potential privilege escalation or denial-of-service attacks stemming from the affected functions.

item.title: Red Hat Issues libX11 Update for RHEL 8.6 Support
item.description: Red Hat issued a libX11 security update for RHEL 8.6 Advanced Mission Critical and Extended Update Support, fixing several X11 client library flaws. The update is rated Important, with CVSS scores via CVE links, but no active exploitation has been seen. Red Hat recommends applying the patch promptly to mitigate privilege escalation or denial-of-service risks from the affected functions.

item.title: MongoDB CVE-2026-118383 Causes Failover Crashes
item.description: A pre‑authentication flaw in MongoDB Server (CVE‑2026‑118383) lets attackers send two crafted requests that crash the database when a lagging replica is promoted to primary. The crash occurs only if the server still lacks recent changes, making failover a trigger for the denial‑of‑service condition. MongoDB released patched versions earlier this week; administrators should upgrade immediately to prevent service disruption.

item.title: GitHub Repos Hit by Credential‑Stealing Malware
item.description: A threat actor used stolen GitHub credentials to push a credential‑stealing payload into tens of thousands of repositories since November 10, targeting GitHub Actions secrets. In 1,800 repositories, the malware ran and exfiltrated secrets; Aikido named the campaign wfx‑loot and identified 4,837 compromised accounts. Users should revoke compromised tokens, audit repository access, and enable multi‑factor authentication to stop further theft.

item.title: Red Hat Quay Flaw Enables Private Image Theft
item.description: A critical flaw in Red Hat Quay lets attackers steal private container images, overwrite repositories, and maintain persistent access. The vulnerability permits unauthorized read and write operations on image repositories, potentially exposing sensitive code and facilitating further lateral movement. Red Hat recommends applying the latest Quay patch or upgrading to a supported version to stop data exfiltration.

item.title: Maersk Data Theft Confirmed by WhiteArmor
item.description: WhiteArmor ransomware group claims to have stolen 100GB of data from Maersk during a $5 million extortion attempt. The breach involved exfiltration of shipping‑industry operational data, but no evidence shows ransomware execution or system compromise. Maersk should conduct a forensic investigation, reset compromised credentials, and strengthen access controls to mitigate further exfiltration.

item.title: .NET 11 Introduces Supply Chain Security Enhancements
item.description: Microsoft released .NET 11, a Standard Term Support release, adding C# 15, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, and Windows development features. The update introduces changes to software supply chain integrity, authentication handling, and platform lifecycle to reduce future attack vectors. Defenders should adopt .NET 11 and plan migrations from unsupported .NET 8/9 to benefit from these security improvements.

item.title: Node.js HTTP/2 Flaws Crash Servers, Leak Data
item.description: Unauthenticated clients can crash Node.js servers using HTTP/2 on 24.x and 26.x lines, and a second flaw leaks memory containing responses for other connections. The flaw stems from improper HTTP/2 frame handling, enabling denial of service and cross‑connection data exposure without authentication. Node.js released patched versions 22.23.5, 24.22.3, and 26.13.1; upgrade immediately to stop crashes and leaks.

item.title: GitHub Accounts Hijacked, Secret-Stealing Malware Deployed
item.description: A threat actor hijacked 4,837 GitHub accounts and pushed a secret‑stealing payload into 61,764 repositories, targeting secrets in GitHub Actions. The actor used stolen credentials to gain unauthenticated write access, enabling malware to exfiltrate CI pipeline secrets without user interaction. GitHub issued a security advisory, urging token revocation, two‑factor authentication, and repository scans for malicious code.

item.title: Palo Alto PAN-OS Enables Root Code Execution
item.description: A PAN-OS Panorama RCE flaw lets authenticated admins run arbitrary code with root privileges. CVE-2026-0330 exploits improper privilege checks during configuration, enabling full system compromise; no public exploit yet. Apply the critical November 11 patch for Panorama and update Cloud NGFW, Prisma Access, and standalone PAN-OS immediately in all affected environments.

item.title: PCI DSS 4.0 Compliance Tool Rankings Released
item.description: Cyber Security News released a comparative guide evaluating ten top compliance platforms designed for PCI DSS 4.x standards. The analysis reviews platforms across scope-reduction architecture, continuous technical controls, merchant management, and Qualified Security Assessor assessment automation stacks. Organizations subject to payment card security standards should review these tool benchmarks to streamline audit preparation and continuous control compliance.

item.title: Cyber Security News Ranks Top Risk Management Platforms
item.description: Cyber Security News published a review ranking ten leading IT and cybersecurity risk management platforms for enterprise governance. The evaluation scored tools based on workflow effectiveness, tracking risk intake, treatment, exception management, and financial risk quantification capabilities. Security teams can evaluate these platform rankings to optimize risk register tracking, streamline accountability, and improve overall risk remediation workflows.

item.title: GitHub Discusses Accountability for AI Patch Flaws
item.description: GitHub’s Agentic Autofix can fix one vulnerability while creating another, raising accountability questions for patches. The tool re‑runs detection engines and project tests after patching, but can miss side effects, requiring validation and metric monitoring. Security teams should adjust CISO policies before deploying the agent, select models, and apply continuous testing to mitigate flaws.

item.title: Hackers Abuse Windows Group Policy to Deploy Citrus Ransomware and Disable Microsoft Defender
item.description: A new ransomware group called Citrus is using Windows Group Policy to push its malware across entire company networks and switch off Microsoft Defender first. Group Policy is a trusted Windows tool that admins use to manage many computers at once.

item.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
item.description: Starting Tuesday, an attacker used stolen credentials for 4,837 GitHub accounts to plant a secret stealer in repositories those accounts could write to, according to Aikido Security, a security software company. The stealer is built to take the secrets and cloud credentials that a repository's CI workflows can reach.

item.title: Red Hat Freerdp Update Addresses Important Vulnerability
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the freerdp component on its Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support platform. The update addresses an important vulnerability, rated by Red Hat as Important, though the specific CVE identifiers are not listed in the advisory. Users should apply the update immediately to mitigate potential exploitation risks.

item.title: Red Hat httpd:2.4 Update Covers Important Vulnerability
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the httpd:2.4 module on Enterprise Linux 8.6 Advanced Mission Critical and Extended Update Support platforms. The advisory marks the update as Important, implying a CVSS score in the 7.0-8.9 range, though specific CVE IDs are not listed. Users should apply the update immediately to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Important Update for httpd:2.4
item.description: Red Hat issued an important security update for the httpd:2.4 module on RHEL 8.4 AMCS and EUS LLA platforms. The update addresses multiple vulnerabilities with CVSS scores indicating significant risk, though specific CVE identifiers are referenced in the advisory. Security teams should apply the patch immediately to mitigate potential exploitation and maintain compliance with Red Hat’s security guidance.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important Update for aspell
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for the aspell package on RHEL 9.6 Extended Update Support. The advisory covers multiple vulnerabilities with CVSS scores indicating significant risk, with CVE references provided in the documentation. Administrators should apply the patch promptly to prevent exploitation and align with Red Hat’s security maintenance schedule.

item.title: CISOs and OT Engineers Disagree on Cyber Resilience
item.description: According to a SANS survey, CISOs and engineers disagree on operational technology resilience during IT compromises. While all surveyed security chiefs expect facilities to maintain output using manual controls, only 15% of engineering practitioners express confidence in process survival. Industrial organizations should align leadership expectations with frontline engineering capabilities to improve manual operational procedures and threat response plans.

item.title: Critical Apache HTTP/2 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code Remotely
item.description: A critical flaw in Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module, mod_http2, can let a remote attacker run code on the server. Tracked as CVE-2026-119618, it affects versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and is fixed in version 2.4.71, released yesterday. Only servers with HTTP/2 enabled are affected, according to Red Hat, which ships the server as part of Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

item.title: ScreenConnect Targeted 288 Endpoints via Rogue Clients
item.description: ConnectWise reported unauthorized access incidents affecting at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations using ScreenConnect with rogue client extensions. The company disabled five third‑party extensions in partner environments, noting no evidence of infrastructure compromise or software vulnerability in ScreenConnect itself. Security teams should monitor for rogue client activity, enforce extension whitelisting, and review access controls to mitigate similar threats.

item.title: SCKit Worm Compromises ScreenConnect Panels, Infects 288 Devices
item.description: Attackers leveraged the SCKit worm to compromise cloud‑hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect panels, infecting at least 288 endpoints across 48 organizations. The worm exploited unauthorized panel access to deploy rogue ScreenConnect clients, establishing session‑cookie relays for persistence and remote control. Security teams must audit credentials, enforce MFA, terminate unverified clients, and apply vendor updates to block further exploitation.

item.title: Node.js Fixes 16 Security Flaws That Could Expose TLS Private Keys and Crash Servers Remotely
item.description: The Node.js project has released fixes for 16 security flaws across its 22.x, 24.x and 26.x lines. The official advisory says the patched builds are v22.23.5, v24.22.3 and v26.13.1. The update also refreshes three bundled parts: llhttp, undici, and sqlite.

item.title: MongoDB Use‑After‑Free CVE‑2026‑118383 Exploited
item.description: MongoDB is affected by CVE‑2026‑118383, a use‑after‑free vulnerability that can lead to arbitrary code execution in enterprise environments. The flaw arises when the database fails to release memory after a malicious request, allowing attackers to trigger a crash or execute injected code. MongoDB has released a patch; administrators should apply the update immediately and monitor logs for anomalous activity.

item.title: Apache RCE Flaw CVE-2026-119618 Requires Immediate Patch
item.description: A remote code execution flaw identified as CVE-2026-119618 targets Apache servers, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code in enterprise environments. The vulnerability stems from improper input validation in the request handling module, and public proof‑of‑concept exploits demonstrate its feasibility. Patch is available immediately; apply the latest Apache release or vendor‑issued hotfix and enable recommended detection rules.

item.title: Falcon C2 Targets Government Portals with JavaScript
item.description: Falcon C2 malware is targeting government portals by injecting malicious JavaScript into web pages. The injected scripts exploit client‑side vulnerabilities, capture user input, and establish command‑and‑control channels to exfiltrate data. Security teams should block known malicious domains, enforce script‑blocking policies, and immediately apply vendor security patches to mitigate the threat.

item.title: Git Six Flaw RCE Patches Released
item.description: Git released patches for six critical flaws that could enable remote code execution if an attacker crafts malicious repository data. The vulnerabilities involve deserialization of untrusted input and were identified through root‑cause telemetry and detection rule hunting. Security teams should apply the Git patches immediately and review detection rules to ensure coverage of the affected code paths.

item.title: Ivanti RCE Flaw CVE-2026-121683 Demands Prompt Patch
item.description: Ivanti software contains a remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-121683, that permits attackers to run arbitrary code on affected systems. The flaw originates from unchecked user input in the configuration parser, and publicly available proof‑of‑concept code confirms exploitation. Security teams should immediately apply the Ivanti patch or upgrade to the latest release and enable the vendor‑issued detection rules.

item.title: Fireworks AI Incident Exposes Notion Chat Data
item.description: Notion experienced a data breach stemming from a security incident involving Fireworks AI, exposing user chat data. The incident allowed unauthorized access to sensitive chat telemetry and conversational records through third-party platform integration. Security teams must review root-cause telemetry, deploy threat detection rules, and apply recommended patches to secure impacted integrations.

item.title: ScreenConnect RCE Flaw Threatens Managed Service Providers
item.description: ScreenConnect, a support platform used by managed service providers, contains a remote code execution flaw that could allow attackers to execute arbitrary commands. The vulnerability arises from insufficient input validation in the session initiation module, and proof‑of‑concept exploits demonstrate its feasibility. Apply the vendor‑issued patch immediately, update to the latest ScreenConnect version, and enable the detection rules to mitigate risk.

item.title: WhiteArmor Ransomware Targets Maersk Shipping
item.description: WhiteArmor ransomware infected Maersk's network, exfiltrating sensitive data before encrypting files. The malware leveraged credential theft and lateral movement, exploiting unpatched Windows services, causing operational disruption and potential data loss. Maersk should apply vendor-supplied patches, isolate affected systems, enforce multi-factor authentication, and conduct forensic analysis to mitigate further spread.
